story: UPDATE of No.93. DeepGreen's FERC application P-15423 named AEA's Cook Inlet PowerLink its Strategic Partner, DeepGreen's October 27th answer concedes no partnership or interconnection agreement, and AEA's October 15th cable RFI is still prequalifying suppliers for a December 2031 in-service target, as the comment window closed November 2nd

claims.claim: The Alaska Energy Authority published its CIPLink submarine cable prequalification and request for information, numbered 27025, on October 15th.
claims.notes: WebFetched listing. Project title 'CIPLINK COOK INLET POWER LINK-HVDC PROJECT', RFI# '27025', Published Date '10/15/2026', document link /Home/File/10618. The document itself reads 'PQ/RFI Release October 15, 2026' (Table 1). This is recent background: it predates No.93's October 22nd date but was first reported by Petroleum News on October 25th.

claims.claim: Responses to AEA's CIPLink cable RFI are due December 15th at 2 p.m. Alaska time.
claims.verbatim: 12/15/2026 @ 2:00pm Alaska Time
claims.notes: WebFetched listing. The RFI document repeats 'PQ/RFI Response Deadline December 15, 2026, 2:00 p.m. Alaska time', and Petroleum News (October 25th) says 'required by 2 p.m. on Dec. 15'. The listing also confirms a pre-response conference on November 4th, 10:30 a.m. Alaska time, at AEA's Anchorage office with a Teams option. Written questions are due November 25th.

claims.claim: AEA engaged Stantec Consulting Services in July 2025 to support CIPLink development, and that work produced the cable RFI.
claims.verbatim: In July 2025, AEA engaged Stantec Consulting Services Inc. (Stantec) to support the CIPLink Project development.
claims.notes: Read from the showrunner's local text extraction of the public PDF (out/2026-11-02/ciplink_rfi.txt, section 2.1). The cover reads 'Prepared by: Stantec Consulting Services', and section 2.1 continues 'This work has resulted in this PQ and RFI.' Petroleum News doesn't mention Stantec.

claims.claim: AEA's RFI says it is not an invitation to bid, an offer or a commitment to proceed with procurement.
claims.verbatim: It does not constitute an invitation to bid, an offer, or a commitment to proceed with procurement
claims.notes: Local extraction, Notice to Respondents (page 1). The document seeks supplier qualifications, technical information and budgetary pricing from HVDC submarine cable suppliers and installers (section 1.1). Taken together, these show that no cable supplier has been contracted yet. Say so as an inference from AEA's own document, not as a quote.

claims.claim: AEA's RFI describes CIPLink as an HVDC system crossing Cook Inlet between Beluga and Nikiski.
claims.verbatim: by crossing the Cook Inlet between Beluga and Nikiski.
claims.notes: Local extraction, section 2.1. DeepGreen's application uses the same endpoints ('between Nikiski and Beluga').

claims.claim: AEA says CIPLink has received federal funding through the Department of Energy's Grid Resilience and Innovation Partnerships program.
claims.verbatim: AEA has received federal funding for CIPLink through the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE's) Grid Resilience and Innovation Partnerships (GRIP) Program.
claims.notes: Local extraction, section 2.1. Curly apostrophes normalized to straight. The amount, $206.5 million, comes from AEA's project page (C29). The RFI says Buy America, Build America rules apply because the project is partly federally funded.

claims.claim: The base bid for CIPLink's submarine cable is a 100 MW asymmetrical monopole.
claims.verbatim: The base bid installation is a 100 megawatt (MW) asymmetrical monopole.
claims.notes: Local extraction, section 2.1. Petroleum News (October 25th) independently reports 'The initial transmission line would have a capacity of 100 megawatts'. This is the main qualifier on the '200 MW' figure that DeepGreen's application and AEA's project page use (C27, C37).

claims.claim: A second 100 MW pole, which would make a 200 MW bipole, is bid only as an additive alternate.
claims.verbatim: The additive alternate provides a second 100 MW pole for a 200 MW bipole configuration.
claims.notes: Local extraction, section 2.1. Section 2.3.1 adds that if the alternate isn't awarded, the cable sizing and spacing must still accommodate future expansion to 200 MW. Petroleum News calls it 'the potential for a later expansion to 200 megawatts'.

claims.claim: AEA's RFI puts the CIPLink submarine cable route at about 40 miles, or 64 km, from landfall to landfall.
claims.verbatim: The submarine cable route length is approximately 40 miles (64 km), landfall to landfall.
claims.notes: Local extraction, section 2.1. Unit check: 64 km is 39.8 miles, so the figures agree. Petroleum News also says '40-mile'. AEA's project page (C26), AEA's FERC motion and DeepGreen's application all say 38 miles. Don't reconcile the two. Cite each figure with its own source and say the RFI measures landfall to landfall.

claims.claim: The RFI places CIPLink's southern converter station at Soldotna, about 28 miles by terrestrial line from the cable landfall near Nikiski.
claims.verbatim: The terrestrial line from the southern, Soldotna converter station to the submarine cable landfall location near Nikiski has a route length of approximately 28 miles (45 km).
claims.notes: Local extraction, section 2.1. Unit check: 45 km is 28.0 miles. The northern Beluga converter station is expected to be less than 3 miles from the Beluga landfall. This bears on DeepGreen's claim to be 'co-locating with the CIPLink southern terminal' (C38), because the RFI's southern converter station is at Soldotna and Nikiski is only the landfall.

claims.claim: AEA is targeting an in-service date of December 2031 for all CIPLink components.
claims.verbatim: AEA is currently targeting an in-service date of December 2031 for all components of the CIPLink HVDC Project.
claims.notes: Local extraction, section 2.2. This is a target, not a commitment. Petroleum News says 'targeting the system going into service in 2031.' AEA's project page gives 'Target Completion: 2032', which fits the GRIP deadline in C12.

claims.claim: AEA's RFI says the federal GRIP funding requires CIPLink to be fully completed by August 31st, 2032.
claims.verbatim: GRIP funding requires that the CIPLink HVDC Project be fully completed by August 31, 2032.
claims.notes: Local extraction, section 2.2. Petroleum News corroborates: 'The federal funding requires project completion by August 2032.'

claims.claim: AEA expects to take the submarine cable engineering, supply and installation procurement to market in mid-2027.
claims.verbatim: expected to be issued to the market mid-2027
claims.notes: Local extraction, section 2.2. Section 3 says a competitive procurement, if conducted, 'is expected to be initiated about June 2027', and AEA reserves the right to negotiate directly instead. Petroleum News says 'mid-2027'.

claims.claim: AEA plans to award the submarine cable contract at the end of 2027.
claims.verbatim: with contract award planned for the end of 2027
claims.notes: Local extraction, section 2.2. This is the cleanest primary support for saying CIPLink's cable has no supplier yet: AEA's own planned award is about a year away.

claims.claim: AEA's schedule has submarine cable and accessory manufacturing finished by the end of 2029.
claims.verbatim: Submarine cable and accessory manufacturing are to then be completed by the end of 2029
claims.notes: Local extraction, section 2.2. Planned, not achieved.

claims.claim: AEA's schedule has the submarine cable installed in 2030 and 2031.
claims.verbatim: followed by the submarine cable installation work in 2030 and 2031.
claims.notes: Local extraction, section 2.2. Planned, not achieved.

claims.claim: AEA intends to complete CIPLink's environmental review and permit issuance in early 2029.
claims.verbatim: The environmental review process and permit issuance is intended to be completed early 2029.
claims.notes: Local extraction, section 2.3.2. The same section says AEA plans marine surveys within the year, that the route is subject to change, and that alternative routes are expected to be analyzed during permitting.

claims.claim: The RFI specifies a rated DC voltage of plus or minus 100 kV for the CIPLink submarine cable.
claims.verbatim: Rated DC voltage, Uo ±100 kV
claims.notes: Local extraction, electrical requirements table (section 2.3.1). Table cells joined with a single space. The same table gives rated DC current as '1000 A', and the dedicated metallic return as an assumed 30 kV. Sanity check: 100 kV times 1000 A is 100 MW, matching the monopole rating (C07). The table labels inside the document are numbered inconsistently (the text calls it Table 1, the caption calls it Table 2).

claims.claim: The cable route must cross at least three existing assets, namely GCI's Kodiak Kenai Fiber Link, Alaska Communications' AKORN cable and Hilcorp's Tyonek W10 pipeline.
claims.verbatim: For the submarine cable installation, a minimum of three crossings need to be considered
claims.notes: Local extraction, section 2.3.2 and the Preliminary Crossing Information table: '1 Kodiak Kenai Fiber Link (KKFL) GCI Communication Corp ASN', '2 ACS Alaska-Oregon Network (AKORN) Alaska Communications SubCom', '3 Tyonek W10 Pipeline Hilcorp Harvest Alaska LLC'.

claims.claim: The RFI says CIPLink's preliminary cable route runs adjacent to and west of the planned route of a proposed LNG line.
claims.value: west of a proposed LNG line
claims.verbatim: The preliminary routing is also adjacent (west of) the planned routing of a proposed liquified natural gas (LNG) line
claims.notes: Local extraction, section 2.3.2, continuing 'coordination with the LNG project will be ongoing.' The RFI doesn't name the LNG project. Don't name it in the deck without another source.

claims.claim: Respondents prequalify for future cable procurement with a score of 24 or more out of 40 and no category below 4.
claims.verbatim: Respondents with a score of 24 or more (an average rating of "good" or better) with no category scored less than 4 will be deemed prequalified.
claims.notes: Local extraction, section 3.1. Curly quotes normalized. There are four equally weighted criteria scored 0 to 10, 'resulting in a possible 40 points'.

claims.claim: AEA's RFI notes there are noise limits in Cook Inlet because of marine mammals.
claims.verbatim: as there are noise limits in the Cook Inlet due to marine mammals.
claims.notes: Local extraction, section 5.3, asking respondents for noise information on installation equipment. This is AEA's own project, not DeepGreen's. It parallels Cook Inletkeeper's noise argument against DeepGreen (C51) and shouldn't be presented as AEA taking a side.

claims.claim: AEA's RFI asks cable bidders how they would prevent ice scouring damage at the landfalls.
claims.verbatim: methods of preventing damage at landfall locations from ice scouring.
claims.notes: Local extraction, section 5.3, in the context of 'high current tidal arctic environments'. Other verified design specs not carried as separate claims: post-lay burial depth of 3 feet, HDD landfalls of 0.6 miles with a maximum depth of 65 feet, 48 single-mode fibers, and a 40-year minimum design life.

claims.claim: AEA's CIPLink project page lists the project status as In Development.
claims.verbatim: Status: In Development
claims.notes: WebFetched. The page is undated, so date_of_source is the fetch date during this run. The long URL https://www.akenergyauthority.org/What-We-Do/Railbelt-Energy/Cook-Inlet-PowerLink-Project redirects here.

claims.claim: AEA says CIPLink would eliminate the current single point of failure between Kenai and Anchorage.
claims.verbatim: would eliminate the current single point of failure between Kenai and Anchorage
claims.notes: WebFetched. This is the owner's stated purpose, a prospective benefit, so attribute it to AEA.

claims.claim: AEA's project page describes CIPLink's subsea cable as 38 miles long.
claims.verbatim: a 38-mile subsea cable
claims.notes: WebFetched. AEA's October FERC motion also says 38 miles, and so does DeepGreen's application (C37). The October 15th RFI says 'approximately 40 miles (64 km), landfall to landfall' (C09), and Petroleum News says 40. The two figures differ, probably because of different endpoints or route revision. Don't merge them.

claims.claim: AEA says CIPLink would deliver up to 200 megawatts of bidirectional power transfer.
claims.verbatim: deliver up to 200 megawatts of bidirectional power transfer
claims.suggested_hedge: up to 200 MW, with 100 MW in the cable base bid
claims.notes: WebFetched. The fetched sentence reads 'The system would, deliver up to...' with a stray comma, so only the clean substring is quoted. Keep 'up to'. The RFI's cable base bid is 100 MW, and 200 MW is an additive alternate (C07, C08).

claims.claim: AEA's project page puts CIPLink's estimated cost at $413 million.
claims.verbatim: Estimated Cost: $413 Million
claims.notes: WebFetched. Petroleum News (October 25th) independently says 'The estimated cost of the project is $413 million'. ARITHMETIC CHECK: the page's three funding lines ($206.5M grant + $62.5M secured + $142.5M additional required) add to $411.5 million, not $413 million. That is a $1.5 million difference on AEA's own page. Don't present a summed total and don't imply the pieces add to $413 million.

claims.claim: AEA's project page lists a federal Department of Energy grant of $206.5 million for CIPLink.
claims.verbatim: Federal DOE Grant: $206.5 Million
claims.notes: WebFetched. The RFI identifies the program as DOE GRIP (C06). See C28 on the funding arithmetic.

claims.claim: AEA's project page lists $62.5 million for CIPLink as secured.
claims.verbatim: Secured: $62.5 Million
claims.suggested_hedge: AEA lists $62.5 million as secured in addition to the federal grant
claims.notes: WebFetched. The page doesn't say whether this line includes the grant. Petroleum News says '$269 million has been secured to date' (C33), which equals $206.5M + $62.5M. That suggests the $62.5 million is secured on top of the grant. This reading is our arithmetic, so don't state it as AEA's.

claims.claim: AEA's project page lists an additional $142.5 million as still required for CIPLink.
claims.verbatim: Additional Required: $142.5 Million
claims.notes: WebFetched. $413M minus Petroleum News's $269M secured is $144M, not $142.5M. The same $1.5 million difference noted in C28. Use AEA's figure as printed, attributed to the page.

claims.claim: AEA's project page gives CIPLink a target completion of 2032.
claims.verbatim: Target Completion: 2032
claims.notes: WebFetched. The page also reads 'Timeline: Eight Years'. This fits the RFI's December 2031 in-service target and August 31st, 2032 GRIP deadline (C11, C12).

claims.claim: Petroleum News reported that $269 million of CIPLink's estimated $413 million had been secured, citing AEA.
claims.verbatim: The estimated cost of the project is $413 million, of which $269 million has been secured to date, AEA says.
claims.suggested_hedge: according to Petroleum News, citing AEA
claims.notes: WebFetched. Byline Alan Bailey, Contributing Writer, October 25th. This is a secondary write-up of the RFI and AEA figures. $269M equals AEA's $206.5M grant plus $62.5M secured (C29, C30). It also corroborates the 40-mile line, the 100 MW initial capacity, the 2031 service target, the August 2032 federal deadline, mid-2027 procurement and December 15th responses.

claims.claim: DeepGreen's application gives the project an installed capacity of 100.0 megawatts.
claims.verbatim: The project would have an installed capacity of 100.0 megawatts.
claims.source_outlet: DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC, FERC eLibrary
claims.notes: Background (filed before the window). Read from the showrunner's local extraction (out/2026-11-02/ferc/app_20260211.txt, draft notice of application, item j). eLibrary pages are JavaScript-rendered and return no content to WebFetch, so the local file is the verification path. Agrees with No.93 C01.

claims.claim: DeepGreen's application describes the project as a firming load for the Railbelt grid via the planned CIPLink.
claims.verbatim: The project is designed as a "firming" load for the Alaska Railbelt Grid via the planned Cook Inlet PowerLink (CIPLink)
claims.source_outlet: DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC, FERC eLibrary
claims.notes: Local extraction, draft notice item j. The sentence continues 'providing carbon-free baseload-equivalent energy for co-located high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure.' This is the applicant's framing. AEA's motion quotes it back.

claims.claim: DeepGreen's application says its landing site is strategically positioned to interface with AEA's CIPLink.
claims.verbatim: The landing site is strategically positioned to interface with the Alaska Energy Authority's (AEA) Cook Inlet PowerLink (CIPLink)
claims.source_outlet: DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC, FERC eLibrary
claims.notes: Local extraction, Exhibit 1 section 3. Apostrophe normalized. The original continues with an em dash into the CIPLink description, so the verbatim stops before it.

claims.claim: DeepGreen's application describes CIPLink as the planned 38-mile, 200 MW HVDC subsea line between Nikiski and Beluga.
claims.verbatim: the planned 38-mile, 200 MW HVDC subsea transmission line between Nikiski and Beluga.
claims.source_outlet: DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC, FERC eLibrary
claims.notes: Local extraction, Exhibit 1 section 3. This matches AEA's own '38-mile 200-MW' wording in its FERC motion and the project page. AEA's later RFI says about 40 miles landfall to landfall, with only 100 MW in the base bid (C07, C09).

claims.claim: DeepGreen's application says the hub would co-locate with the CIPLink southern terminal.
claims.verbatim: By co-locating with the CIPLink southern terminal, the DeepGreen Hub serves as a primary renewable energy source and a "firming" load for this state-priority infrastructure
claims.source_outlet: DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC, FERC eLibrary
claims.suggested_hedge: DeepGreen's application claims it would co-locate with
claims.notes: Local extraction, Exhibit 1, Public Interest Benefit. TENSION: DeepGreen's landing zone is in the Nikiski Industrial Corridor, between Agrium and Kenai LNG. AEA's RFI puts CIPLink's 'southern, Soldotna converter station' about 28 miles by land from the Nikiski landfall (C10). Report DeepGreen's words as its claim only. The RFI doesn't map the exact Nikiski landfall, so don't assert a distance between the two sites.

claims.claim: DeepGreen asked FERC for a 48-month preliminary permit term.
claims.verbatim: The Applicant requests a permit term of 48 months to allow for multi-seasonal environmental baseline studies and complex silt-scour engineering.
claims.source_outlet: DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC, FERC eLibrary
claims.notes: Local extraction, Initial Statement item 5. Agrees with No.93 C08, which also records that DeepGreen's September 21st answer called it a 'three-year permit period'.

claims.claim: DeepGreen's study schedule places its interconnection and CIPLink technical studies in months 24 to 36 of the permit term.
claims.verbatim: IV Interconnection & CIPLink Technical Studies 12 Months Months 24-36
claims.source_outlet: DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC, FERC eLibrary
claims.notes: Local extraction, Exhibit 2 table. Cells joined with spaces, '&' rendered as '&', and the en dash in 'Months 24-36' changed to a hyphen per the house rule. Agrees with No.93 C13. Don't convert the months to calendar years, because no permit has been issued and no start date exists.

claims.claim: DeepGreen estimates its studies over the 48-month permit term would cost $4,500,000.
claims.verbatim: The Applicant estimates the total cost of the investigations and studies for the 48-month permit term to be $4,500,000.
claims.source_outlet: DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC, FERC eLibrary
claims.notes: Local extraction, Exhibit 2. This is the applicant's own estimate, which says it is in a 'pre-development' phase initiating a Series A private placement. Scale check: $4.5 million against CIPLink's $413 million estimated cost, which is the owner's figure. These are different things (studies versus construction) and shouldn't be compared as like for like.

claims.claim: The filing summary in DeepGreen's draft notice lists CIPLink and the Alaska Energy Authority as its Strategic Partner.
claims.verbatim: Strategic Partner: CIPLink (Alaska Energy Authority)
claims.source_outlet: DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC, FERC eLibrary
claims.notes: Local extraction, draft notice 'Filing Summary for Cook Inlet'. AEA's October motion quotes the line: 'identifies "CIPLink (Alaska Energy Authority)" as a "Strategic Partner."' Agrees with No.93 C18.

claims.claim: DeepGreen's October 27th answer says it has not entered into, and does not claim to hold, any formal binding partnership, co-sponsorship or executed interconnection agreement with AEA.
claims.verbatim: Applicant has not entered into, nor does it claim to hold, any formal binding partnership, co-sponsorship, or executed interconnection agreement with AEA.
claims.source_outlet: DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC, FERC eLibrary
claims.notes: Read from the local extraction (out/2026-11-02/ferc/answer_20261027.txt, section III.B). The sentence is preceded by 'Applicant agrees with and confirms AEA's clarification for the record:'. Signed '/Louis Wolfson/', Managing Member, dated October 27th. This is new relative to the September 21st answer (No.93 C31), which disclaimed a 'formal agency agreement' but didn't mention an interconnection agreement.

claims.claim: DeepGreen's answer says its references to CIPLink reflect conceptual engineering alignments and regional transmission possibilities under study.
claims.verbatim: References to AEA's planned Cook Inlet PowerLink (CIPLink) in the application reflect conceptual engineering alignments and regional transmission possibilities under study.
claims.source_outlet: DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC, FERC eLibrary
claims.notes: Local extraction, section III.B. Apostrophe normalized. The next sentence says the permit's purpose is to study 'whether such an interface is technically and economically viable.'

claims.claim: DeepGreen's answer asks FERC to issue the preliminary permit for Project No. P-15423-000.
claims.verbatim: 3. Issue the preliminary permit for Project No. P-15423-000.
claims.source_outlet: DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC, FERC eLibrary
claims.notes: Local extraction, section IV. The answer also asks FERC to grant the motions to intervene of the City of Kenai, Cook Inletkeeper, AEA and Rebecca Long, and to 'Dismiss the objections seeking permit denial'. It says it doesn't oppose those four interventions. It names only four of the seven movants, though its service list includes all seven.

claims.claim: DeepGreen told FERC a preliminary permit authorizes zero physical hardware placement and zero construction.
claims.verbatim: a preliminary permit authorizes zero physical hardware placement, zero construction, and zero thermal or material discharge into Cook Inlet.
claims.source_outlet: DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC, FERC eLibrary
claims.notes: Local extraction, section III.C. This is consistent with FERC's own notice (C61) and with AEA's motion ('a preliminary permit would neither authorize construction nor approve an interconnection'). Alaska's News Source (October 28th) paraphrases the same answer.

claims.claim: DeepGreen's answer says the City of Kenai has not taken an opposing position on the application.
claims.verbatim: Applicant notes that the City has not taken an opposing position to the application
claims.source_outlet: DeepGreen Cook Inlet SPV LLC, FERC eLibrary
claims.notes: Local extraction, section III.A. This is DeepGreen characterizing the city's motion. I didn't read the City of Kenai's own motion (20261013-5302), so attribute it strictly to DeepGreen.

claims.claim: The Alaska Energy Authority told FERC it has had no communications or relationship with DeepGreen.
claims.verbatim: AEA has had no communications or relationship with DeepGreen and will continue to clarify that fact as this proceeding develops.
claims.notes: Background. Read from the local extraction (out/2026-11-02/ferc/20261008-5007.txt, section II.B). Dated October 7th, filed October 8th, signed by general counsel Mark Billingsley. AEA says it wants the record accurate on references to AEA and CIPLink, and takes no position for or against the permit. Agrees with No.93 C24.

claims.claim: AEA told FERC it owns the Sterling to Quartz Creek transmission line.
claims.verbatim: AEA owns the Sterling-Quartz Creek transmission line
claims.notes: Local extraction, section II.C. The en dash between Sterling and Quartz Creek is changed to a hyphen per the house rule. AEA says these lines are critical to delivering Bradley Lake power.

claims.claim: AEA told FERC it holds capacity rights on the Soldotna to Sterling transmission line.
claims.verbatim: holds capacity rights on the Soldotna-Sterling transmission line.
claims.notes: Local extraction, section II.C. En dash changed to a hyphen.

claims.claim: Cook Inletkeeper told FERC it opposes issuing the preliminary permit because of potential impacts on Cook Inlet beluga whales, their habitat and the watershed.
claims.verbatim: Inletkeeper opposes the issuance of a preliminary permit due to concerns about the potential impacts on Cook Inlet Beluga whales, their habitat, and the health of the watershed.
claims.notes: Read from the local extraction (out/2026-11-02/ferc/20261026-5031.txt, section IV). The document is dated October 23rd and signed by co-executive director Bridget Maryott. The eLibrary filed date is October 26th (C56). The motion also says 'No filings related to the Project have acknowledged the NMFS acoustic harassment threshold for continuous noise', and puts the beluga population at 'fewer than 400 individuals'. DeepGreen's answer confirms that Inletkeeper opposes the permit.

claims.claim: FERC's eLibrary listed 262 filings in docket P-15423 dated on or before November 2nd.
claims.verbatim: filed on or before 2026-11-02: 262
claims.suggested_hedge: as of the evening of November 2nd
claims.notes: This is a count taken at about 21:50 Alaska time on November 2nd (06:50 UTC November 3rd) from FERC's keyless eLibrary AdvancedSearch API. Verbatim from the showrunner's census (out/2026-11-02/ferc_census.txt). I couldn't re-run it independently: the eLibrary search page is JavaScript-rendered and returns nothing to WebFetch, and the raw ferc_hits.json is a single 190k-token line too large for line-level spot-checks. The API reported 285 total hits, including 23 dated November 3rd that are excluded here. 244 of the 262 are typed only as Comment on Filing. The count will keep moving as late filings post.

claims.claim: The docket held 134 filings dated on or before October 22nd, the date of the previous deck.
claims.verbatim: filed on or before 2026-10-22 (No.93's date): 134
claims.notes: Same census and same method caveat as C52. Cross-check: No.93's own listing, retrieved October 22nd at 22:20 Alaska time, held 135 entries (No.93 C21 notes). That is one more than 134, a plausible difference from accession-versus-document counting or a re-dated entry. Use 134 only as stated by this census, which means 128 more filings had arrived by November 2nd.

claims.claim: 72 filings in docket P-15423 are dated November 2nd, the final day of the comment window.
claims.verbatim: filed on 2026-11-02 alone: 72
claims.suggested_hedge: at least 72, as counted that evening
claims.notes: Same census and caveat as C52. eLibrary dates electronic filings received after 5 p.m. Eastern to the next business day, which likely explains the 23 filings dated November 3rd. That is our understanding of FERC practice, not stated in the census.

claims.claim: Seven parties filed eight motions to intervene in docket P-15423, namely the Center for Biological Diversity, the Alaska Commercial Fisheries Conservation Alliance, the Kenai Peninsula Borough, Rebecca Long, AEA, the City of Kenai and Cook Inletkeeper.
claims.verbatim: That is 7 movants in 8 motions.
claims.notes: Census lists each motion with accession: CBD 20260901-5211 (September 1st), ACFCA 20260914-5093 and 20260915-5024 (the second with a protest), KPB 20260914-5074, Rebecca Long 20261005-5140, AEA 20261008-5007, City of Kenai 20261013-5302, Cook Inletkeeper 20261026-5031. Independent corroboration: DeepGreen's October 27th answer's service list names exactly these seven parties, and I read the AEA and Inletkeeper motions directly.

claims.claim: Cook Inletkeeper's motion to intervene was filed on October 26th, the last of the eight motions.
claims.verbatim: 10/26/2026 20261026-5031 Motion to Intervene of Cook Inletkeeper, AK under P-15423.
claims.notes: Census line. The document itself is dated and certified 'October 23, 2026'. Use October 26th as the filed date and don't write 'filed October 23rd'.

claims.claim: No competing application or notice of intent to file one appeared in the P-15423 record by the November 2nd deadline.
claims.verbatim: No filing carries a competing-application or notice-of-intent document type.
claims.suggested_hedge: no competing application appears in the record as of the evening of November 2nd
claims.notes: This claims an absence, judged by eLibrary document type across all 285 hits including the November 3rd postings. A competing application could in principle be docketed under a new project number, which this docket search wouldn't show, so state it as 'in the record' only.

claims.claim: FERC set 5 p.m. Eastern Time on November 2nd as the deadline for comments, motions to intervene and competing applications on DeepGreen's permit.
claims.verbatim: by 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time on November 2, 2026
claims.source_outlet: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, notice in the Federal Register
claims.notes: WebFetched. Background. The notice is dated September 1st and published September 4th (FR Doc 2026-18151, Vol. 91 No. 171). Agrees with No.93 C40. 5 p.m. Eastern is 1 p.m. Alaska time, which is our conversion.

claims.claim: FERC's notice describes the project as about 330 to 350 marine hydrokinetic turbines.
claims.verbatim: approximately 330-350 marine hydrokinetic turbines utilizing a proprietary universal docking cradle system
claims.source_outlet: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, notice in the Federal Register
claims.notes: WebFetched. The notice also lists '66 modular subsea-compute hives (data center pods)'. Alaska's News Source (October 28th) carries both figures, quoting the federal filing.

claims.claim: FERC's notice describes an approximately 3.5-mile, 115 kV subsea cable from the hub to a landing site in the Nikiski Industrial Corridor.
claims.verbatim: an approximately 3.5-mile long, 115 kV hybrid power/fiber-optic armored subsea cable
claims.source_outlet: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, notice in the Federal Register
claims.notes: WebFetched. The landing site is 'within the Nikiski Industrial Corridor' 'positioned between the Agrium Kenai Nitrogen Operations and the Kenai Liquefied Natural Gas Plant'. Alaska's News Source repeats the 3.5-mile, 115 kV figures. Scale contrast: DeepGreen's own cable is about 3.5 miles at 115 kV AC-class, while CIPLink is a roughly 38 to 40-mile ±100 kV HVDC crossing. Don't conflate the two cables.

claims.claim: FERC's notice says the sole purpose of a preliminary permit is to give the holder priority to file a license application.
claims.verbatim: The sole purpose of a preliminary permit, if issued, is to grant the permit holder priority to file a license application during the permit term.
claims.source_outlet: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, notice in the Federal Register
claims.notes: WebFetched. The notice adds 'A preliminary permit does not authorize the permit holder to perform any land-disturbing activities or otherwise enter upon lands or waters owned by others without the owners' express permission.' Do NOT use the notice's '100 megawatts' of 'estimated annual generation', which is a unit error (see killed).

claims.claim: Kenai Peninsula Borough Mayor Peter Micciche told Alaska's News Source that sloppy was how he would describe DeepGreen's approach at this stage.
claims.verbatim: Sloppy is the way I would describe this approach at this stage in the game,
claims.notes: WebFetched twice, and the quote was identical both times. Byline Rebecca Palsha, published October 28th, 2:07 PM AKDT. Quote it as 'Sloppy is the way I would describe this approach at this stage in the game.' The borough is itself an intervenor (20260914-5074). The article also reports, in the reporter's words and not as a quote, that 'he hasn't gotten an email, letter or a phone call from DeepGreen.'

claims.claim: Under a proposed exchange, Hilcorp would sell Enstar 1.2 billion cubic feet of gas previously allocated to MEA, no later than December 15th.
claims.verbatim: sell to Enstar 1.2 billion cubic feet of gas previously allocated to MEA
claims.suggested_hedge: according to Petroleum News, Enstar has asked the RCA to approve
claims.notes: RUNNER-UP STORY. WebFetched. Byline Alan Bailey, November 1st. The date comes from 'Hilcorp Cook Inlet would, no later than Dec. 15, 2026, sell to Enstar 1.2 billion cubic feet'. Correction to the brief: the seller is Hilcorp, and the gas comes from MEA's allocation. Enstar has applied to the RCA for approval, which hasn't been granted. Single secondary source: I didn't fetch the RCA filing, so no primary document.

claims.claim: The exchange gas would be priced at $9 per mcf plus a $2.75 per mcf fee paid by Enstar to Hilcorp.
claims.verbatim: The gas would be priced at $9 per mcf, plus a $2.75 per mcf fee that Enstar would pay to Hilcorp
claims.notes: RUNNER-UP. WebFetched. The page says '$9', not '$9.00'. Don't add the two figures into a single price, because the article presents them separately.

claims.claim: Without the exchange, Enstar would have about 3.7 billion cubic feet of gas in storage by the end of December.

claims.suggested_hedge: Enstar projects, according to Petroleum News
claims.notes: RUNNER-UP. WebFetched. This is a projection. The article ties the proposal to Enstar 'anticipating a shortfall in its gas supply portfolio.' The Gas Watch house rule bars safety verdicts, so present this only as Enstar's projection.

claims.claim: Petroleum News reports that Enstar's typical stored gas range is 6 billion to 7 billion cubic feet.
claims.verbatim: That is substantially lower than the utility's typical stored gas range of 6 billion to 7 billion cubic feet.
claims.notes: RUNNER-UP. WebFetched. Apostrophe normalized. Units agree with C66 (both in Bcf).

claims.claim: Enstar would have to deliver equivalent payback volumes to MEA's storage account by March 31st, 2028.

claims.notes: RUNNER-UP. WebFetched. The full phrase is 'Enstar is obligated to deliver equivalent payback volumes to MEA's account'. These are proposed terms pending RCA approval.

killed.claim: CIPLink's submarine cable has no supplier.
killed.why: AEA's RFI doesn't say this in those words. It is an inference from the RFI seeking supplier qualifications, with award planned for the end of 2027. Use C04 and C14 and attribute the inference, e.g. 'AEA is still prequalifying cable suppliers and plans an award at the end of 2027'.

killed.claim: AEA's funding lines add up to CIPLink's $413 million estimated cost.
killed.why: Arithmetic fails. $206.5M grant + $62.5M secured + $142.5M additional required = $411.5M, not $413M. Never present a summed total from AEA's page.

killed.claim: DeepGreen's landing site co-locates with CIPLink's southern terminal.
killed.why: Supported only as DeepGreen's own assertion (C38). AEA's RFI puts the southern converter station at Soldotna, about 28 miles by land from the Nikiski landfall. Don't state co-location as fact.

killed.claim: CIPLink is a 200 MW line, without qualification.
killed.why: The RFI's cable base bid is 100 MW, and 200 MW is only an additive alternate. Write 'up to 200 MW' or '100 MW initially, expandable to 200 MW'.

killed.claim: Cook Inletkeeper filed its motion to intervene on October 23rd.
killed.why: October 23rd is the date on the document and its certificate of service. The eLibrary filed date is October 26th (C56).

killed.claim: DeepGreen's project would generate 100 megawatts annually.
killed.why: Unit error in FERC's notice ('estimated annual generation ... 100 megawatts'). Megawatts measure capacity, not annual energy. Use the application's '100.0 megawatts' installed capacity (C34).

killed.claim: Micciche said 'I haven't gotten an email, letter or a phone call from DeepGreen.'
killed.why: This is the reporter's paraphrase ('He says he hasn't gotten...'), not a verbatim quote. It may be reported in indirect speech attributed to Alaska's News Source, but never in quotation marks.

killed.claim: CIPLink will be in service in December 2031.
killed.why: This is a target, not a fact. AEA says it is 'currently targeting' that date, and its project page says 2032. Use 'AEA is targeting' (C11).

killed.claim: The census counts (262, 134, 72) were independently re-verified line by line against the raw API JSON.
killed.why: Not done. The eLibrary search page returns no content to WebFetch, and ferc_hits.json is one 190k-token line too large to Read in part. The counts stand as the showrunner's recorded measurement, at confidence 0.87 to 0.88 with an as-of hedge. The movant list (C55) is independently corroborated by DeepGreen's service list.
